– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,

Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failure occurs because calling CSVRecord.toMap() triggers a NullPointerException on records created using a CSVFormat with no headers. Inspecting the toMap() method shows it simply calls putIn() with a new HashMap and returns the result. The putIn() method iterates over the mapping field entries and populates the map with corresponding values by column index. However, the mapping field is a Map<String, Integer> containing the header-to-column index relationships. When the CSV format has no header, this mapping is null. In putIn(), the code attempts to iterate over mapping.entrySet(), causing an NPE because mapping is null. According to the bug report, the method contract states a null map should be returned instead of throwing an NPE when no headers are present.

The underlying problem is that the CSVRecord instance does not have a non-null mapping when headers are not defined, resulting in putIn() throwing an NPE due to no null check on mapping before iteration.

Hence, to fix this bug, CSVRecord should handle the case of no headers by either initializing mapping to an empty map or guarding methods like putIn() and toMap() against null mapping. This would ensure toMap() returns an empty map rather than throwing an exception, aligning with the documented behavior.

Recent bug reports do not directly mention this issue but relate to headers or mapping inconsistencies, confirming that the header-related logic is a fragile area.

Next step: It is best to look at how CSVRecord mapping is constructed or set during parsing or CSVRecord construction and whether any null checks or defaults are applied there. Also, checking the CSVParser and CSVFormat interactions with headers might help but the primary fault is in CSVRecord's toMap/putIn assuming mapping is never null.

messages.content:
The initializeHeader() method in CSVParser returns null as the headerMap when the CSVFormat has no header array set (formatHeader is null). This results in CSVParser.headerMap remaining null.

Later, the CSVRecord instances created during parsing hold a reference to this headerMap as their mapping. When the format has no header, mapping is null in CSVRecord. The toMap() method on CSVRecord calls putIn(), which tries to iterate over mapping.entrySet() but mapping is null, causing the NullPointerException.

The bug report explicitly states that if no header is defined, toMap() should return a null map (likely meaning an empty map) rather than throw an NPE. The current implementation does not handle null mapping gracefully.

In summary, the absence of a header leads to initializeHeader() returning null, which becomes a null mapping in CSVRecord. The putIn() method doesn't guard against null mapping, so calling toMap() on such records throws NPE.

To fix, the code should either ensure initializeHeader() returns an empty map instead of null when no header is present, or CSVRecord.putIn() and toMap() should check for null mapping before usage and return an empty map accordingly. This aligns with the method documentation and expected behavior.

This is the root cause of the failing test testToMapWithNoHeader which tries to call toMap() on a record from a format with no headers.
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The NullPointerException occurs in CSVRecord.toMap() due to the internal mapping field being null when CSVFormat has no headers defined. The toMap() method delegates to putIn(), which iterates over mapping.entrySet() without null-checking mapping. The mapping is derived from the CSVParser's headerMap initialized in initializeHeader(), which returns null if the CSVFormat's header array is null (indicating no headers). This causes CSVRecord.mapping to be null. According to the bug report, toMap() should return an empty map in this case, not throw an NPE. The root cause is the missing null check or non-null default for mapping in putIn() and toMap(). To fix, either initializeHeader() should return an empty map instead of null, or putIn()/toMap() should check for null mapping before iterating.

Suggested fix locations:
- CSVParser.initializeHeader()
- CSVRecord.putIn(java.util.Map)
